page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running on an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor with an x86_64 architecture and a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the average tier across most standard compute and memory tests. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core Geekbench score of 1320.0 and a multi-core score of 5074.0, while the Passmark CPU score is recorded at 9658.56. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 465.34 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 51.09 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In database operations, the instance handles 7.99 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a Passmark database score of 3169.42. However, it exhibits poor performance for medium-sized LLM inference, processing only 11.93 prompt tokens per second and 6.39 text generation tokens per second on a 7B model.

The ecs.hfr7.2xlarge offers a balanced, dedicated hardware profile with high memory density, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The absence of local storage means users must rely on network-attached storage, which is constrained by the 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. This instance is highly suited for in-memory databases like Redis, relational database hosting, static web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications. It is not recommended for heavy machine learning or large-scale LLM inference due to the lack of hardware accelerators and weak CPU-based inference benchmarks.
